feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 1 (score 69.32) and iteration 4 (same design, score 69.32 again) are the evidence, and this candidate is the same design, so you should expect the same score. Iteration 3 showed that y=0.03 m cost about 10 points with the same controller, so keep y=0.05 m. Iteration 2 showed that the 16 mm footprint lowered the score to 54.45 with the controller held fixed, so keep 12 mm. Line loss has stayed at about 1 per run through iterations 0 to 4 (1.0 to 1.65 per run), so the span and footprint have only partly reduced it. Steering oscillation has stayed between 0.09 and 0.15, so it is not the limiting factor. Do not treat any of this as a result for the current candidate. Next, the span is the open question: iteration 5 tested ±0.04 m only if the geometry is revisited, and that result is not yet in. Body width does not move the off-track limit, which is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) = 0.06 m across the allowed range, so do not use it as a lever.
requested_changes: Hold sensor_size at 0.012 m and the forward offset at y=0.05 m, because iteration 2 (16 mm) and iteration 3 (y=0.03 m) both scored below the 69.32 reference.
If the span test (±0.04 m, iteration 5) lowers line_loss_events clearly below about 1 per run, test a single later change of ±0.05 m at y=0.05 m. If not, keep the ±0.03 m span.
Keep wheel track, wheel radius, mass and body fixed, since the evidence does not point at them.
